report.source_text: Ultrasound-guided biopsy (Figure 3) showed diffuse proliferation of large, atypical cells with clear cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and prominent nucleoli (Figure 4). Immunohistochemistry analysis demonstrated positive staining for CD-20, a B-cell marker (Figure 5) and Ki-67 staining showed a proliferation index of 60-70% (Figure 6). Further immunohistochemistry analysis showed atypical cells that stained positive for CD-45, BCL-6, and CD-10 but were negative for Her-2-neu, ER, PR, MUM-1, CD-30, ALK, and C-MYC.

report.source_text: The patient underwent left heme port placement and completed six cycles of Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Hydroxydaunorubicin, Oncovin, and Prednisone (R-CHOP) chemotherapy. Currently, the patient is in remission and continues to have no recurrence, confirmed with a normal mammogram and no suspicious lesions on FDG-PET/CT scan at a two-year follow-up appointment.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Stage IV, diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old Hispanic woman presented with a palpable 2 cm left breast mass in the upper outer quadrant (axillary tail of Spence) with overlying yellow discoloration and no axillary lymphadenopathy on initial exam. Mammography revealed an oval mass with indistinct margins at the 1 o'clock position, 13 cm from the nipple. Ultrasound confirmed an oval mass measuring 16 x 11 x 15 mm with indistinct margins and no regional lymphadenopathy on ultrasound alone. Ultrasound-guided biopsy demonstrated diffuse proliferation of large atypical cells with clear cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemistry showed CD20+, CD45+, BCL-6+, CD-10+ staining with Ki-67 proliferation index of 60-70%, and negative staining for Her-2-neu, ER, PR, MUM-1, CD-30, ALK, and C-MYC, confirming diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Staging FDG-PET/CT revealed extensive metastatic disease: diffuse osseous involvement of appendicular and axial skeleton, left breast mass with ipsilateral axillary lymph node involvement, bilateral pulmonary spiculated nodules with ground-glass opacities, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, liver involvement, and abdominal lymphadenopathy (mesenteric, retroperitoneal, and left common iliac chain), establishing stage IV disease. The patient underwent left heme port placement and completed six cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy, achieving remission with no recurrence at two-year follow-up.
